label: Race day evening: in a Pullman car back to London, Holmes explains to Ross and Watson
quote: We had the corner of a Pullman car to ourselves that evening as we whirled back to London

label: Race day evening: the train reaches Clapham Junction
quote: This is Clapham Junction, if I am not mistaken

label: Race day evening: arrival at Victoria, in less than ten minutes (expected)
quote: we shall be in Victoria in less than ten minutes

label: Race day evening: a cigar with the Colonel in Holmes and Watson's rooms (offered)
quote: If you care to smoke a cigar in our rooms, Colonel
note: Holmes's invitation; the story does not say whether Ross comes.

label: Monday evening: curried mutton is served at Straker's house and a dish set aside for the stable-boy
quote: The opium was added after the dish was set aside for the stable-boy
note: Holmes: only Straker and his wife could have chosen curried mutton for supper that night.

label: Monday evening: the opium is added to the stable-boy's dish (Holmes's reasoning)
quote: The opium was added after the dish was set aside for the stable-boy
note: Holmes asks which of Straker and his wife had access to the dish without the maid seeing them; so before she carries it down.

label: Monday night: Simpson, in his flight from the stables, drops his cravat (Holmes's account)
quote: Simpson in his flight had dropped his cravat

label: Monday–Tuesday night: Straker picks up the cravat (Holmes's account)
note: Holmes guesses he meant to use it in securing the horse's leg. The text does not say exactly when or where he found it.

Holmes (¶219–220): Straker went down in the dead of the night and took out Silver Blaze; the dog, knowing him, did not bark enough to wake the lads. Hunter locked the door when he ran out (¶31); the door was found open at seven.

label: Monday–Tuesday night: Straker leads the horse out to the hollow, where his light would be invisible (Holmes's account)
quote: Straker had led out the horse to a hollow where his light would be invisible

note: Holmes (¶226): Straker had already, in spite of the rain, taken off his overcoat to do his delicate task. No wind that night (¶96).

label: Monday–Tuesday night: in the hollow, Straker gets behind the horse and strikes a light (Holmes's account)
quote: Once in the hollow, he had got behind the horse and had struck a light

note: Holmes (¶226): frightened at the glare, the horse lashed out and its steel shoe struck Straker on the forehead; as he fell, his knife gashed his thigh. Then the horse bolted (¶231).

label: Straker practises the tendon-nicking on the sheep (Holmes's surmise)
quote: would not undertake this delicate tendon-nicking without a little practice
note: Holmes's surmise, which the lame sheep bear out; not dated.

label: Straker leads a double life as "Derbyshire", with a second establishment and an extravagant wife who runs him into debt
quote: an excellent customer of the name of Derbyshire, who had a very dashing wife
note: Holmes's conclusion (¶225) and the milliner's word (¶229); not dated, before the Monday night.

label: After returning to London: Holmes calls on the milliner with Straker's photograph
quote: When I returned to London I called upon the milliner
note: Between the night train back and the return from the race; not ordered against the trip to Winchester more finely.
